messages:
jamie: Heads-up — after the ESM-first SDK roll, a partner reported huge client bundles and a runtime crash on Cloudflare Workers: `TypeError: (0 , _index.createClient) is not a function`.

noor: ugh, familiar. Did you check if the entrypoint accidentally became a namespace import at bundle time? Some bundlers rewrite named exports if they hit a CJS interop shim.

jamie: We shipped `type: module` and removed the CJS index. Our `package.json` has `sideEffects: false` to keep bundles small. But apparently the runtime initializer that attaches `globalThis.__rw__` lives in a small file only imported for side effects.

sam: Two things to watch: 1) re-export patterns (e.g. `export * from './runtime'`) can hide side-effect-only imports, 2) sideEffects:false will allow bundlers to drop files that only run for their side effects.

jamie: Here's a minimal repro I gave the partner: `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk';` + deploy to workers with esbuild. Worker errors on cold start. Node consumer is fine.

noor: Quick checklist: - open npm tarball (`npm pack`) to confirm dist files - inspect `exports` map in package.json - check that the side-effect file is imported from the top-level entry (not just conditionally)

sam: We hit an annoying interplay: to keep tree-shakable modules, we moved debug helpers into register file. But when consumers run bundlers for edge, those bundlers remove register because nothing references its exports. That broke the client factory which expects some runtime shims.

jamie: I tried two fixes locally: A) add `"sideEffects": ["./dist/register-globals.js"]` B) make the entry import the register file once: `import './register-globals.js'; export * from './runtime.js';`

noor: Which worked?

jamie: Both made the crash go away. But with A the partner reported +140KB gzip increase. With B the bundle stayed small because register file is tiny after refactor.

sam: Long-term: keep `sideEffects:false` and ensure any side-effectful initialization is either 1) explicitly imported from the entry, or 2) provided as an explicit subpath export like `redwood-sdk/edge-init`. The latter gives consumers control but is more docs overhead.

noor: Also watch named vs default exports. If your ESM build emits `export default` and your CJS build uses `module.exports =`, bundlers create interop wrappers (`__toModule`) that confuse tree-shakers. Prefer named exports for public API: `export function createClient(){}` and have CJS build `exports.createClient = createClient` (via rollup/tsc).

jamie: Good point — our `dist/index.cjs.js` had `module.exports = require('./runtime.cjs').default;` which meant some consumers imported default, others expected named. Created subtle runtime mismatch in rollup builds.

sam: CI/regression idea: add a smoke job that runs an esbuild/webpack rollup bundle of the sample-app and asserts: 1) bundle size < threshold, 2) the bundled code can run under a minimal edge-like env (node with globalThis polyfill) and calling createClient returns a function.

jamie: I'll add a GH action that uses `esbuild --bundle sample/app/edge-entry.ts --format=esm` and then runs `node --input-type=module -e "import('./out.js').then(m=>console.log(typeof m.createClient))"` to assert it's `function`.

noor: Docs follow-up: add a short DX note on the SDK README about packing ESM/CJS parity, `sideEffects` pitfalls, and an `edge` export suggestion. Also update the quickstart template to show `import 'redwood-sdk/edge-init';` at the top of edge handlers so copy/paste works.

build-bot: quick build: sample-app edge smoke (pr/489) passed — bundle 72KB gzipped, createClient detected as function. https://ci.company/builds/1623

sam: Another mitigation: keep runtime init pure and dependency-free (no heavy dev-only deps) so marking it side-effectful doesn't bloat bundles. Move debug/inspector code behind dynamic import.

jamie: Action list I will follow: - refactor register -> minimal `edge-init` without deps - export `./edge-init` subpath and update quickstart - keep `sideEffects:false` and ensure entry explicitly imports edge-init for the default path - add CI esbuild smoke test

noor: Happy with that plan. If anyone hits a customer repro, point them to `redwood-sdk/edge-init` for now.

jamie: Thanks y'all, will open PR and tag reviewers. :rocket:
